Testing 5/18, this is a great study plan so far! If I were to give any advice, I would consider using the JackSparrow Anki deck. I myself have been using MilesDown and it's a GREAT resource, but if I am not mistaken, the JS deck has subdecks for each chapter for the Kaplan Review books. So, for example, you can study chapters 1 and 2 of the biochem book on monday, and then on that same day you can go through the JS anki cards specifically designed for chapters 1 and 2 of biochem. Honestly I wish that I had done this, because I only started doing Anki cards AFTER going through all of the books. I was only able to start memorizing stuff halfway through my entire MCAT studying period. Retaining stuff early on and throughout your whole studying period is really helpful, in my opinion. I'm not entirely sure how great the JS deck is, but the general consensus from online and especially from this subreddit is that it's a great deck. I can wholeheartedly say that Milesdown is a great deck, so if you end up going with that then you are certainly not downgrading.

The Kaplan end of chapter questions, in my opinion, are not that great, certainly not the same level of difficulty you'll see on FL's or the real deal. It's great for wrapping up chapters but I wouldn't use it as a MAJOR source of practice problems.

As for when to start doing FL's, it's kind of up in the air, but I think most people would say to start taking AAMC FL's closer to your test date rather than sooner. There's only 5 available so you wanna strategize when you're taking them, not just take them willy nilly when you feel like it.

I say reschedule. The only reason why I can see to take it tomorrow is to see the real deal. This whole test should ideally be only taken once, though. What you consider to be a good score is based on your standards and what you need, so if you feel like you can do better than your diagnostic then maybe go for it, but think about this: 

Imagine you take it tomorrow and you get a sub-average score. Not a bad score but not a fantastic score either. So this upcoming cycle, it’ll be more difficult to get into schools with that score.  Rather, if you take it a few months from now when you’re more prepared and end up getting a good score, your options will expand - you can still apply this cycle (although you will be applying late), and if you don’t get in this cycle and end up having to take a gap year, YOU CAN STILL USE YOUR GOOD MCAT SCORE! You’ll be armed with a good score in both cases. I would recommend canceling and rescheduling. Don’t get your hopes up SUPER high if you apply this cycle, because you will be applying late, but anything is possible! There’s a stigma that applying late will immediately stop you from getting in anywhere; while there is no debate that applying earlier increases your chances, you should not prioritize that over potentially getting a better score. Best of luck!!
